requestedActions.title: List active task titles from the connected Todoist account, including pagination

guide.summary: Read-only OAuth access to the connected Todoist account is documented via the data:read scope, which covers tasks but is broader than tasks alone. Active tasks are listed with GET /api/v1/tasks using cursor pagination. Provider review and distribution requirements are not documented in the supplied sources.
guide.recommendation: The requested API test is not ready yet. Resolve the access mapping for List active task titles from the connected Todoist account, including pagination. Use “Find missing request” or add official documentation beside that action.

findings.title: Authorization request uses the authorization URL with a scope parameter and response_type=code
findings.detail: Redirect the customer to the authorization endpoint with the chosen scope; the callback then performs the code-to-token exchange.
findings.appliesWhen: Applies to the customer's individual Todoist account authorization.

evidence.quote: https://app.todoist.com/oauth/authorize?client_id = 0123456789abcdef & scope = data:read,data:delete & state = secretstring & response_type = code
Redirect users to the authorization URL at the endpoint

findings.title: data:read grants read-only access to application data including tasks
findings.detail: Request data:read to list active tasks. It is documented as read-only but also covers projects, labels and filters.

evidence.quote: data:read Grants read-only access to application data, including tasks, projects, labels, and filters.

findings.title: Do not request data:read_write or other write scopes for this read-only use case
findings.detail: data:read_write adds write access and includes task:add and data:read, so it is not needed for listing and must be avoided.
findings.appliesWhen: Applies because the app must never create, update, complete or delete tasks.

evidence.quote: data:read_write Grants read and write access to application data, including tasks, projects, labels, and filters. This scope includes task:add and data:read scopes.

findings.title: No narrower task-only OAuth scope is documented in the supplied sources
findings.detail: The narrowest documented grant for task reads is data:read, which the app cannot further restrict. Disclose this to customers as a provider limitation.
findings.appliesWhen: Applies to customer consent wording for the read-only task list.

evidence.quote: data:read Grants read-only access to application data, including tasks, projects, labels, and filters.

findings.title: Task listing is cursor-paginated and needs the same parameters on every page
findings.detail: The first request omits cursor; subsequent requests pass next_cursor as cursor with unchanged parameters.
findings.appliesWhen: Applies when the customer has more active tasks than one page.

evidence.quote: To fetch the first page of results, make a request without a cursor parameter:
Subsequent Requests To fetch the next page, include the cursor parameter with the value from next_cursor :
Important : Always use the same parameters (filters, sorting, etc.) when using a cursor. Changing parameters between paginated requests may result in unexpected behavior or errors.

steps.title: Prepare the OAuth authorization request for data:read
steps.detail: Build the authorization URL with scope=data:read, response_type=code and a state value. Implement the callback to exchange the code for a token only after consent.
steps.doneWhen: Authorization URL with scope data:read is built and a redirect URI is registered for the test app.

steps.detail: Sign in with the developer's own test Todoist account and approve data:read. Confirm the callback receives a code and the exchange returns an access token.
steps.doneWhen: Token exchange succeeds for the test account with data:read granted.

steps.title: List the first page of active tasks
steps.detail: Call GET /api/v1/tasks with limit=50 and the OAuth bearer token, without a cursor parameter, to fetch the first page. Representative input: limit 50. Expected result: a results array where each task has id and content (the task title). Boundary check: confirm the token grants only data:read with no write scopes and that the request log shows only GET calls.
steps.doneWhen: The first page returns results with id and content fields and the request log contains only GET requests.

evidence.quote: To fetch the first page of results, make a request without a cursor parameter:
get /api/v1/tasks https://api.todoist.com /api/v1/tasks

fields: YOUR_TOKEN: OAuth access token from test authorization

steps.title: Fetch continuation pages of active tasks
steps.detail: Repeat GET /api/v1/tasks with cursor set to the next_cursor value from the previous response, keeping limit=50 and all other parameters unchanged. Collect the content of each page's tasks. Stopping condition: continue until the documented end of pagination is reached; the supplied passages do not quote a rule, so do not stop after two pages or on an empty page. Boundary check: confirm only GET requests are sent and no write endpoint is called.
steps.doneWhen: Pages are followed with cursor and all task titles are collected only after a documented end condition is verified from the API documentation; this step is not complete until that stop rule is confirmed.
